findings.claim: Sterling's E-Infrastructure segment revenue accelerated 174% YoY in Q1 2026 (company-wide revenue +90%); segment is now ~60% of total revenue at ~24% margin and is guided for 40%+ full-year 2026 revenue growth, driven by hyperscaler/AI data-center demand.
findings.source: Yahoo Finance - "Will Sterling's 125% Data Centre Growth Extend Into 2026?", https://finance.yahoo.com/news/sterlings-125-data-centre-growth-152200180.html

findings.claim: Sterling raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $3.7-3.8 billion (a 20% increase from the prior guidance midpoint); signed backlog climbed 78% YoY to $3.8 billion and combined backlog rose 131% to $5.2 billion, with total visibility near $6.5 billion — management attributes this to Sterling's integrated site-development-plus-electrical positioning (via the CEC acquisition) strengthening its competitive standing as data-center capex expands.
findings.source: Yahoo Finance - "Sterling and Data Centers: The Integrated Buildout Trade", https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/sterling-data-centers-integrated-buildout-150700712.html

findings.claim: Sterling's identified competitors in mission-critical/data-center construction include Quanta Services and EMCOR (both also reporting robust hyperscaler-driven demand), plus Fluor, Granite Construction, Skanska USA, MasTec, AECOM, Kiewit, Webcor and Turner — a broad field of large diversified peers rather than a single disruptive new entrant.
findings.source: ZoomInfo - "Sterling Infrastructure Competitors & Alternatives (2026)"; Yahoo Finance - "3 Infrastructure Stocks Fueling the Data Center Building Boom"

findings.claim: YTD 2026 stock performance shows Sterling (STRL) +68.7% vs closest AI-infrastructure comp Comfort Systems (FIX) +77.4%, while Quanta Services +49.5% and EMCOR +22.6% — all outperforming the Zacks Construction sector (+7-11%) and S&P 500 (+10.9-11.8%), but Comfort Systems specifically outpacing Sterling on the same AI-buildout theme.
findings.source: Zacks via Yahoo Finance - "Sterling vs. Comfort Systems: Which AI Infrastructure Stock Wins?", https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/sterling-vs-comfort-systems-ai-135400134.html

findings.claim: No direct evidence found of any named Sterling customer actively adding a second/competing site-development or electrical contractor, or bringing that scope of work in-house. The 2026 hyperscale data-center GC market instead remains concentrated among a small set of program managers (Turner, DPR, Mortenson, Hensel Phelps, Holder, Clayco) with specialized MEP subcontractors (e.g., Rosendin Electric) self-performing the electrical package (30-40% of total construction cost) — i.e. the observed industry pattern is trade-specialist self-performance within GC-led teams, not owner-side insourcing away from contractors like Sterling.
findings.source: Buildermuse - "Top 20 Data Center Construction Contractors in 2026", https://buildermuse.com/commercial/the-top-20-data-center-construction-contractors/; Maktinta - "Who Builds AI Data Centers (and Who's Hiring) in 2026", https://www.maktinta.com/post/ai-data-center-construction-and-hiring-2026

findings.claim: At June 30, 2026, Sterling's signed backlog rose 116% year-over-year to $4.3 billion, and combined backlog (signed + awarded not signed) rose 150% year-over-year to $5.6 billion, driven by E-Infrastructure demand.

findings.claim: In Q2 2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026), Sterling's E-Infrastructure segment revenue grew 192% year-over-year and signed backlog grew 165% year-over-year, with mission-critical (data center/semiconductor) projects accounting for 92% of the segment's backlog; legacy site development revenue alone grew 111%.
findings.source: Zacks (via Globe and Mail / TradingView), "Is Sterling's 192% E-Infrastructure Growth Just Getting Started Now?" / "Can Sterling's Backlog Strengthen Its Infrastructure Growth Prospects?"

findings.claim: Following record Q2 2026 results, Sterling raised full-year 2026 guidance, targeting roughly 25% revenue growth for 2026; management ties the outlook to structurally expanding end markets (large-scale data centers, semiconductor fabs, advanced manufacturing) with hyperscaler customers now scoping campus projects lasting up to 12 years.
findings.source: PR Newswire, "Sterling Reports Record Second Quarter Results and Raises Full Year 2026 Guidance"; Seeking Alpha, "Sterling Infrastructure Q2 2026 Review: A Triple Beat Sold On The Mix"

findings.claim: Moody's (per CNBC, 2026-07-24) flagged 'unprecedented' AI capex spending as a threat to hyperscaler credit quality; separately, analysts note the AI capex cycle (aggregate hyperscaler capex ~$700B in 2026, projected ~$820B in 2027 per Moody's, and up to $1.15T cumulative 2025-2027 per Goldman Sachs) could run ahead of monetization -- the bear case is that Sterling's E-Infrastructure demand durability is contingent on hyperscalers continuing to fund a capex cycle that some analysts flag as increasingly debt- and off-balance-sheet-financed rather than purely cash-flow funded.
findings.source: CNBC, "Moody's says 'unprecedented' AI spending threatens credit quality of Amazon, Meta, Alphabet and others", cnbc.com/2026/07/24/moodys-ai-spending-credit-quality-amazon-meta-alphabet.html

items.claim: 2026 revenue guidance raised to $3.7-3.8B, up 20% at the midpoint from prior guidance.
items.quote: Revenue of $3.7 billion to $3.8 billion, which at the midpoint is a 20% increase over previous guidance
items.speaker: Nicholas Grindstaff

items.claim: 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance raised to $18.40-$19.05, up 36% at the midpoint from prior guidance.
items.quote: Adjusted diluted EPS of $18.40 to $19.05, which at the midpoint is a 36% increase from previous guidance
items.speaker: Nicholas Grindstaff

items.claim: Full-year 2026 E-Infrastructure segment revenue is guided to grow 80% or higher including CEC.
items.quote: For the full year 2026, we expect to deliver E-Infrastructure revenue growth of 80% or higher, including the full year contribution of CEC.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Legacy (ex-CEC) E-Infrastructure business is guided to grow approaching 60% or higher in 2026.
items.quote: We anticipate that the legacy business will grow at rates approaching 60% or higher as several of our larger projects accelerate.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: E-Infrastructure adjusted operating profit margin is guided to the mid-20% range for 2026.
items.quote: Adjusted operating profit margins for E-Infrastructure are expected to be in the mid-20% range.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Management expects CEC margins to expand 300-500bp over the next 12-18 months as low-margin end markets are exited.
items.quote: we're still extremely bullish that we're going to see 300 to 500 basis points of margin in really 12 to 18 months
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin hit a first-quarter record of 20%, up more than 150bps YoY.
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled with margins expanding over 150 basis points year-over-year to reach a new first quarter record of 20%.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Management states margin expansion is not coming from raising prices with customers.
items.quote: Everybody keeps asking us if we're getting more price. The answer is no, we're not getting more price.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: CEO describes Sterling's competitive positioning in winning the semiconductor fab campus bid as overwhelming versus other bidders.
items.quote: There was no one else in the room that was going to have a chance at this.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Management expects to become the preferred site-development partner for future U.S. semiconductor fab projects, similar to its position in data centers.
items.quote: we feel very confident that just like in data centers, we will be the supplier of choice for every chip plant that comes out in the future
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Q1 2026 share repurchases totaled $12 million at an average price of $305.14; $362 million remains under the buyback authorization.
items.quote: share repurchases of $12 million at an average price of $305.14 per share. Remaining availability under the existing repurchase authorization is $362 million.
items.speaker: Nicholas Grindstaff

items.claim: Sterling ended Q1 2026 in a net cash position of $224 million ($512M cash vs $287M debt).
items.quote: We ended the quarter with $512 million of cash and debt of $287 million for a cash net of debt balance of $224 million.
items.speaker: Nicholas Grindstaff

items.claim: Management sees a better-quality M&A pipeline now than a year ago and cites balance sheet strength to pursue deals.
items.quote: We are seeing more high-quality acquisition targets in the market today than a year ago. Our significant balance sheet firepower positions us to take advantage of these opportunities.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Sterling signed a lease to triple its modular construction build capacity.
items.quote: We just locked down a lease to triple the size of our modular build capabilities.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: An internal AI deployment aimed at project managers yielded roughly a 15% capacity gain.
items.quote: The AI project we did first was focused on project managers. We picked up about 15% capacity in project managers.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Management emphasizes a risk-averse project selection philosophy as a driver of margin stability.
items.quote: We won't take on high-risk jobs that are going to get us in trouble.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: CEO says the company is turning down customer requests to enter new markets faster than current capacity allows.
items.quote: Right now, our biggest challenge is they would like to have us in 2 or 3 or 4 new markets tomorrow. We've had to say no to some of those.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Hyperscaler customers are urgently pushing Sterling to expand into new geographies faster than before, citing planned capital spending.
items.quote: They're more than pulling now. They're kind of screaming to get into these markets faster with what they see coming in capital spending they're going to do.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Mission-critical projects (data centers, large manufacturing, semiconductor) made up over 90% of E-Infrastructure signed backlog at quarter-end.
items.quote: Mission-critical work, including data centers, large manufacturing projects and semiconductor represented over 90% of E-Infrastructure signed backlog at the end of the quarter.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

items.claim: Signed backlog reached $3.8 billion (+78% YoY) and combined backlog reached $5.2 billion (+131% YoY).
items.quote: Signed backlog at the end of the quarter totaled $3.8 billion, a 78% year-over-year increase and combined backlog grew 131% to reach $5.2 billion.
items.speaker: Joseph Cutillo

qa_flags.question: Given the larger Q1 order intake, how should we think about legacy E-Infrastructure year-over-year growth rates over the remaining 3 quarters to reach the ~60% full-year target?
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO declined to give a quarter-by-quarter breakdown, citing timing variability in project starts and repeating 'I just don't -- I don't have that.'

qa_flags.question: How much do you expect Texas to account for as a percentage of revenue in the site development business (ex-CEC), and where was it last year?
